summaries.demographer: Katherine Holder is a 76-year-old White, non-Hispanic, U.S.-born woman living alone in a 55-and-older condo community in Boynton Beach, Florida (Q08, Q84, Q88, Q89). She has a high school diploma, never married, has no children, and is retired from library aide work (Q65, Q84, Q90). Her household is a single-person household with fixed retirement income from Social Security and savings, and she owns her condo while managing condo fees, insurance, and medical expenses (Q51, Q58, Q74). Her life course reflects mid-century suburban Protestant upbringing, stable family background, work-first education trajectory, and later-life migration to Florida after retirement (Q01, Q02, Q97).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Katherine is highly budget-conscious, risk-averse, and planning-oriented, using checkbook records, spreadsheets, envelopes, emergency savings, and careful prioritization to manage uncertainty (Q17, Q57, Q61). She prefers predictable routines and structured volunteering over spontaneous or chaotic obligations, which reduces cognitive and emotional strain (Q16, Q78). Her spending choices show strong loss aversion and fixed-income caution: she cuts crafts, outings, restaurants, and garden purchases before touching essentials (Q60, Q64, Q82). She still preserves modest discretionary rewards, such as Florida day trips and books, when they fit within a planned allowance (Q62, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Katherine is a regular voter and moderate Democrat with strong civic norms around participation, libraries, Medicare, Social Security, voting rights, and institutional decency (Q23, Q24, Q95). She uses mail ballots, voter guides, and sample ballots, suggesting high procedural trust and careful information processing (Q23). Her politics have become more urgent around democracy, misinformation, racial fairness, and policing accountability, though she expresses these views through discussion, reading, and community programming rather than protest (Q25, Q26, Q29). She is civically embedded through senior center volunteer coordination, library work, church-related service, and neighbor check-ins (Q16, Q47, Q108).
summaries.psychologist: Katherine presents as conscientious, orderly, cautious, compassionate, and independence-oriented, with a self-concept built around reliability and usefulness (Q01, Q16, Q109). She experiences worry, especially about health, finances, hurricanes, and being a burden, but regulates it through lists, routines, walking, phone calls, prayer, knitting, and limiting news exposure (Q43, Q44, Q45, Q50). Her relational style is warm but boundaried: she maintains close family and friendship ties while preserving privacy and living alone (Q05, Q07, Q11). Her motivation centers on generativity in later life, including mentoring volunteers, helping seniors navigate services, making quilts, and preserving family history (Q16, Q65, Q108).
